title: Orchestrator session TTL and probabilistic splitter for model-version pin + rollout interactions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As teams run model-version rollouts (canary and A/B), interactions between session-level pinning, region/tier routing, and fallback model variants produce surprising behaviors: sessions bounce between variants when autoscaling triggers node reassignments, probabilistic canaries get skewed by sticky session caches, and tracing tools show mismatched version attribution for multi-request flows.

Problem statement: We need a routing coordinator that preserves developer intent for: 1) session-level pinning (a user/session should see the same model variant across related requests for a TTL); 2) gradual rollouts via probabilistic split or traffic percentages; and 3) deterministic fallback when capacity/region constraints force degrade paths. The coordinator must be low-latency, consistent across multi-replica serving pools, observable, and reversible (safe rollbacks).

Proposal overview: Implement an "Orchestrator Session Coordinator" (OSC) that sits in the routing layer and is responsible for: (A) assigning and persisting lightweight per-session assignment tokens (not full DB writes) with a configurable TTL; (B) applying a stable probabilistic split function for new sessions tied to a rollout id + salt; (C) honoring region/tier routing constraints and only choosing variants compatible with target SLOs; (D) exposing deterministic fallback ordering when preferred variant isn't available; (E) providing debug tracing and metrics (assignment entropy, per-variant request rates, reassignment events).

Key constraints: 1) Latency overhead must be <= 1ms p50 to not break low-latency SLOs; 2) The OSC cannot rely on synchronous coordination with a centralized DB for every request; 3) It must interoperate with existing session-cookie, API-key, and client-provided session-id inputs; 4) Support for VPC/private deployments where cross-region state sync may be limited.

High-level design: use a hybrid approach: a deterministic split function for first-touch assignment (hash(session-id, rollout-id, salt) -> bucket) combined with an optional short-lived assignment cache (local LRU + distributed sticky cache backed by Dynamo/Redis for hosted where available). The orchestrator will attach a signed assignment token (base64 + HMAC) to the response or include it in an update header, enabling stateless verification and avoiding DB hits for read-mostly flows. If the token is absent, the deterministic split is used. Reassignment occurs only after token TTL expiry or explicit invalidation by rollout controller.

Why different from prior work: Existing tickets mostly focus on affinity or sticky routing. This ticket coordinates three things: short-lived signed tokens (stateless verification), deterministic-first-touch bucket assignment for rollouts, and a graceful fallback policy that prefers in-region, same-tier variants but falls back by scoring compatible variants rather than naive priority lists.
design_notes:
Architecture components: 
- Router plugin (OSC) integrated into the Request Router service. 
- Assignment token format: version|rollout_id|variant|expires_at|salt|signature (base64).
- Deterministic split: 64-bit FNV hash over concatenated inputs, mapped into [0,1) then compared with rollout percentages. 
- Local cache: bounded LRU (configurable size per instance). 
- Distributed sticky cache: optional Redis cluster for hosted (TTL aligned with token TTL). Private deployments can opt-out and rely on tokens + deterministic split. 
- Fallback scoring: score = region_match*R + tier_match*T + model_compatibility*C + recent_error_penalty*E - latency_penalty*L. Tunable weights configured via console. 

Trade-offs considered: 
- Token approach reduces DB lookups but adds header size and slightly increases response payload. Acceptable for text API responses. 
- Full central store gives stronger guarantees for cross-instance stickiness but harms p50 latency. 
- Deterministic split ensures reproducible assignment without state but can't be updated retroactively; token invalidation enables forced reassignment. 
- For session privacy, tokens are signed and contain no PII.

Observability plan: Emit assignment events (assignment.created, assignment.reused, assignment.invalidated, assignment.expired) with labels: rollout_id, variant, region, tier, assignment_ttl_remaining. Add dashboards: per-rollout skew vs target, token hit/miss rate, reassignments timeline, fallback invocations.
acceptance_criteria: OSC assigns initial variant deterministically when no assignment token exists
Assignment token verification succeeds and is used by router to maintain variant across short-lived sessions
Probabilistic split percentages observed in production match configured rollout percentages within 1% after 10k sessions
Fallback scoring chooses in-region compatible variant and falls back gracefully when preferred capacity is unavailable
End-to-end p50 routing added latency <= 1ms, p95 <= 3ms in canary environment
Metrics exist for assignment entropy, token hit rate, and reassignment counts
Migration path documented for Dedicated and Private customers (opt-out to tokenless deterministic only mode)
implementation_plan: Design router plugin API and token schema (PR: core/router#xxxx)
Implement deterministic split module (unit-tested with edge cases)
Add local LRU cache and optional Redis sticky cache layer (feature-flagged)
Wire fallback scorer into route selection path and expose weights in config service
Add metrics/trace points and dashboards (console-team coordination)
Integration tests across multi-region simulator and latency-sensitive harness
Canary rollout to small set of tenants with rollback hooks
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged internal canary in staging for 2 weeks with synthetic traffic and 3 real tenants. Phase 2: Gradual enable 1% of production traffic with automated rollback if reassignment rate > 0.5% or p50 latency regression > 1ms. Phase 3: Open to all tenants, configure token TTL default 30 minutes, console exposes toggle to switch to tokenless deterministic mode for Private deployments. Provide runbook for support to force-invalidate tokens per-rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for hash-split boundary conditions and salt rotations
Property tests to ensure deterministic stability across language/platforms
Integration test with simulated node failures to validate fallback scorer
Load test to verify p50/p95 router latency with LRU cache enabled/disabled
Canary e2e test that checks percentage distribution vs configured target
migration_notes:
- For hosted customers, enable Redis sticky cache by default but allow per-tenant opt-out.
- For Private customers, default to token-only + deterministic split.
- Document API header 'X-Redwood-Assignment' and SDK helpers for reading/writing tokens.
- Provide admin API to invalidate tokens for a rollout id so we can force reassignment during emergency rollbacks.
